item.content:encoded:
Okay so I keep putting off explaining my vote here. I gave this a -1.

[+] Open for my actual thoughts
– hide block

Good things: this is a technical marvel, like I'm really impressed at the level of production that's gone into this, with the custom art, the video and the audio, and the general presentation is supremely pretty.

Unfortunately, the big issue for me is that it reads,,,super blandly? Like particularly the first addendum here which is just, more description, a note the reader has no context for at this point and a newspaper article about a person who again has not been tied into the anomaly here. This means it comes across as a big info-dump of material that doesn't have any meaning for me, or drive the narrative forward.

A lot of the following logs feel like they're lacking the required context for me to understand their significance and it ends up feeling a touch frustrating for me to read. It kinda feels like I'm reading a murder mystery story but from chapter 2, without all the context of the first chapter introducing the victim and the detective and all that. And I mean, I guess on some level this is 'expected' since it's deliberately framed as a mystery for the reader to solve but it feels…unappealing for me personally to want to read or solve.

I've seen this develop from before Arcadia became an official group, going from an idea the author couldn't stop talking about to a draft he wouldn't stop working on until it was just right. The massive effort here is pretty spectacular, along with the multimedia showcase. While there are little bits here and there I would've written differently, the mystery and story at play here are strong and I enjoy reading it even after having seen it through every phase of its development. +1

e: For clarity, I wrote some or all of what's in the final containment procedures and newspaper section, along with probably some other smaller bits throughout, but I do not wish for any sort of co-author credit. Popsioak deserves it all for himself. I just helped around the edges.

item.title: FORGIVE ME, FLAPPER.
item.content:encoded:
Like this piece? See it and many more saplings like it, at Popsioak's Garden, here!

I heard a voice; it said: "e dolore magna gloria
Bring me your heart, and then you will awake
In a state of surprising euphoria
Don't fear the words that I say"

This took a fuckton of time. But! There's a mystery afoot, and all the answers to it are in this document here.
It's my first attempt at writing a puzzle piece, but I think it came out well.
